text:
I would be broke right now if I had ever deposited more than 1-5% of my net worth on margin platforms.

I'm down a bunch from the peak, but in hindsight my discipline in not depositing massive chunks of money (relative to net worth) to try to make losses back is the reason that I am still well positioned relative to how wrong I was on the pathway forward (up) for BTC.

People often talk about counterparty risk, proper, efficient use of capital, and other generic reasons why leverage is a good tool. Its most powerful use case is letting you keep deposits small, which protects you from yourself. I know too many crypto bros who went bust, sometimes multiple cycles in a row, from keeping all their funds on exchanges. They always end up with a monster-sized trade and the rest is history.

I strongly recommend only depositing a fraction to exchanges for trading purposes if you are a speculator. If you lose 1-5%, it generally won't affect your livelihood too much, and it acts as a hard stop you can't bypass on any given position (cheating risk, adding underwater, loosening stops, etc.). 

Another layer, which I learnt from @bitbitcrypto when we sat at the same prop desk, is that you are a different person after a good night's sleep. I remember getting over-obsessed with single bets or a single market phase. So, I would always have a good rest before re-depositing, or wait a certain amount of time. This gives perspective and realigns you with reality after swinging around large amounts of money relative to what you might earn in more traditional jobs. Bonus: take some time to journal in those periods. This will truly help you learn from the past and align with reality.

I tend to be a 'Degen': bet the house too often, over-weight my own conviction then act on it, and bet too big relative to my margin equity. It's double-edged: I will often bust a deposit, but sometimes 100x it. The past 2 years I've happened to bust a lot of deposits, on top of round-tripping millions in unrealized profits. Hard to say what would've happened if BTC had continued to 200-300K in the same trend like I had envisioned. I'd prob be hilariously rich rather than writing this on Twitter.

Leverage trading is heavily path-dependent; timing is everything. Markets will trick you into greed and fear at the worst moments, and believing I am immune to this would be arrogance.

I no longer recommend that people even try to learn trading on leverage. Because I think a lot of my lifetime PnL (most of it in 2021) is simply due to the market I was in going up 100x. I think just buying spot BTC will provide at minimum 10-15x over a decade (probably 5 years IMO). That being said, if you do try your luck, utilize the above trick to cap your downside. Or you won't survive.

tl;dr - deposit small, never re-fill the margin account before a good night sleep.

You will literally die, but not today.

text:
Running an automated book is brutally hard. The robustness needed for backtesting and automation alone is a full-time job. A month of iterating with AI loops plus my own input produced two small but real multi-year edges, and on their own they aren't worth much.

AI will hand you insane-looking strategies if you judge by the backtest, and they are almost guaranteed to be overfit. If a month of AI iteration hands you a Sharpe 2 automated portfolio, it's lying. Split your data into two buckets: five years the AI can research on, and eight months kept sealed. You'll see the same pattern most of the time: beautiful numbers on the five accessible years, invalidated on the eight sealed months.

Finding true edges worthy of automation was way harder than I thought, and required a lot of human input and trader experience to guide my AI so that it didn't mine good-looking numbers without logic.

That experiment taught me five things:

1) There is still edge in human discretion.

2) Simple edges erode, FAST.

3) Combining discretionary angles with statistics, then eliminating (what NOT to do), might be my biggest strength going forward.

4) Anything easily mineable, like simple candlestick and volume patterns, is dry if traded alone.

5) The harder something is to turn into a testable hypothesis, the more edge it can hold.

Your personal read on news, what impact a headline should have versus what it actually does, and what that implies in different scenarios, is one example of discretionary experience.

Or your read on who is currently trading the market, who holds the bag, which counterparty is active, and what unwritten things bother you about a market or feel overblown in the moment.

I believe there's alpha in even simple statistics, which is why I can't post it all. The method though is free: treat a stat like August seasonality as one confluence, not a signal. Alone it's trivia. Stacked with your setups it's edge.

Put simply: the more data points you combine from personal experience, elimination processes, and statistics, the more often you'll find the occasional profitable trade, the kind machines are unlikely to steal.

text:
I think BTC is behaving very similarly to the early 2023 bull run.

Back then we had Alameda and FTX blowing up, and the sentiment was generally ultra-pessimistic. Then there was some notable FUD, including Genesis Global Capital going bankrupt, and fears that Grayscale would have to sell assets as a result, or that Barry would go to jail. Yet I vividly remember being surprised that, on the day of the FUD, markets wouldn't tick further down when I would have expected it most.

A short while later, the breakout from the 16k bottom started happening, and new narratives emerged later on, including BTC ETFs. The key lesson here is that FUD failed to push prices down, and that was a clear sign of seller exhaustion.

I think June was the capitulation, with record ETF outflows, and the FUD that came after (most notably Saylor hammering hundreds of millions of dollars in sales into the 60ks, and Coldcard) was the signal that there are no real sizeable spot sellers anymore. This uptick was bound to happen eventually, whether precipitated by Bessent's comment or something else (it happened sooner than I had expected, thanks to him).

In essence, we're probably at a juncture that I would describe as a major shift. Green dildos are possible! All the wealthy, smart, sidelined capital is asking the question: should I buy BTC again? And when you need to panic buy, it's preferable to be early.

Disable your red buttons; the rest of the year will be green. I think BTC settles somewhere in the 80-100k range before year-end, realistically.
